text.arabic_uthmani: رَّبَّنَا ٱكْشِفْ عَنَّا ٱلْعَذَابَ إِنَّا مُؤْمِنُونَ

words.gloss_range: possessed vocative address, our Lord, with dependence and governing care foregrounded
words.root_gloss_range: broad root range includes lordship, ownership, nurture, repair, gathered groups, staying, and other branches; the local possessed vocative selects lordship with sustaining authority

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the later prepositional phrase marking removal away from the speakers
the later emphatic subject continuing the same collective voice

words.prose: {{ar:رَّبَّنَا}} ({{tr:rabbanā}}) opens the plea by making relation audible before request. The omitted vocative marker does not weaken address; it compresses the cry so the imperative follows from inside dependence. The suffix -nā makes the afflicted group appear first as people bound to their Lord, not first as sufferers or arguers. The root field can range widely, but here the local title selects governing lordship with sustaining care: the speakers appeal to the one who rules their condition to remove the pressure. The word also narrows the earlier lordship thread of Surah 44 into direct first-person address, especially after 44:7 and 44:8. Its doubled opening consonant gives the address a pressed weight before the lighter -nā release. That -nā begins the local chain with {{ar:عَنَّا}} ({{tr:ʿannā}}) and {{ar:إِنَّا}} ({{tr:innā}}), so dependence, exposure, and self-attestation sound like one collective voice.

topics.headline: possessed vocative begins in dependence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the plea begins as direct relational address before it becomes a request.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the word as a possessed noun in vocative direct address before the imperative.

topics.headline: lordship carries governing care
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the request as an appeal to governing lordship and sustaining care, not to a neutral remover.
topics.reason: V4 supports lordship, ownership, and nurture branches for the root, while the local possessed vocative selects the Lord-address branch and does not activate unrelated nominal branches.

topics.headline: surah lordship becomes our-Lord address
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees earlier lordship claims in Surah 44 turn into the afflicted group's own address (44:7; 44:8).
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete same-surah references, and the local suffix changes the lordship topic into first-person possession.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears one collective voice pass through lordship, exposure, and asserted faith.
topics.reason: The first-person plural suffix is repeated locally, and the sound rows describe the long ā cadence without changing the syntax.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the boundary shift from externally described punishment in 44:11 to voiced supplication in 44:12.
topics.reason: The first word of 44:12 carries the first-person possessed voice that converts the prior affected people into speakers.

topics.reason: The phonetic row is local to the surface form and supports the urgency of the opening address.

words.gloss_range: second-person masculine singular imperative asking for direct removal or uncovering of the punishment from the speakers
words.root_gloss_range: broad root range includes removing a cover, exposure, bodily exposedness, open confrontation, and technical disputed branches; the local Form I imperative selects lifting or removing a covering harm

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the preceding vocative addressee of the imperative

words.prose: {{ar:ٱكْشِفْ}} ({{tr:ikshif}}) is grammatically a command, but the addressee has just been named as {{ar:رَّبَّنَا}} ({{tr:rabbanā}}), so the command force becomes urgent supplication. Its 2ms form separates the one who can remove from the first-person plural sufferers, while the pro-dropped subject keeps the requested act in the foreground. The root image makes relief spatial: a covering pressure is to be lifted away, and after the covering punishment of 44:11 the verb asks for reversal rather than vague help. That reversal also has a testing edge: lifting the punishment will expose whether the final faith-claim survives relief, and the same root returns in 44:15 as a divine answer in a different form. The short, clipped imperative is a marked selection, placed before the object so removal becomes the first audible hope before the known punishment is named and before the longer collective phrase follows.

topics.headline: imperative becomes upward supplication
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the urgent command-form is held inside lord-address rather than equal-to-equal ordering.
topics.reason: QAC marks a 2ms imperative, and attachment evidence ties its implicit subject to the preceding vocative addressee.

topics.headline: uncovering reverses the covered condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees relief as the lifting of a covering burden, especially against the punishment condition named in 44:11.
topics.reason: V4 supports the removal-of-cover branch, while the local object and prepositional frame narrow the root to lifting harm rather than bodily exposedness or open hostility branches.

topics.headline: lifting also exposes the faith-claim
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that removing punishment will also reveal whether the stated faith survives relief.
topics.reason: The local sequence moves from request to faith-claim, and the accepted exposure branch can remain as a secondary payoff without replacing the removal sense.

topics.headline: verb organizes the removal frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader follows the plea from addressee to action to separation phrase and then to the punishment object.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence gives the verb an explicit object and a prepositional complement, matching the CRITICAL structural rows.

topics.headline: request anticipates the same-root answer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the command as a forward pressure point because 44:15 answers with the same root in a different form.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows provide the concrete same-surah echo at 44:15, and the local imperative differs from the later participial response.

topics.headline: marked clipped imperative sharpens urgency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the short imperative as a marked and abrupt relief request before the longer collective phrase follows.
topics.reason: The contextual profile marks the exact command form as low occurrence, and the sound-form rows describe the local clipped imperative shape.

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the direct object whose removal is requested

words.prose: {{ar:عَنَّا}} ({{tr:ʿannā}}) gives the imperative its direction: the punishment is to be moved away from us. The preposition primarily marks separation with {{ar:ٱكْشِفْ}} ({{tr:ikshif}}), while the suffix keeps the same afflicted group grammatically present between verb and object. Because it stands before {{ar:ٱلْعَذَابَ}} ({{tr:al-ʿadhāba}}), the endangered speakers are heard before the burden is named; the plea is not abstract removal but removal-from-us. The word also sits in the middle of the -nā chain, and its nasal doubling links the opening address to the final claim with a shared collective sound.

topics.headline: separation phrase marks removal from us
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the request as spatial separation of punishment from the speakers, not only general relief.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the suffix as the prepositional complement of the removal verb, licensing separation-away as the local force.

topics.headline: pronoun binds the affected group
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speakers are built into the grammar of removal rather than added as an explanatory afterthought.
topics.reason: The attached first-person plural suffix is governed locally by the preposition and resumes the same speaker group.

topics.headline: speakers are foregrounded before the burden
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the endangered group before the punishment object, so the plea centers affected people before naming the burden.
topics.reason: The local word order places the prepositional phrase between the imperative and its direct object.

topics.headline: middle -nā carries the collective refrain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the same collective voice in address, exposure, and final assertion.
topics.reason: The repeated suffix and nasal sound are local to the word and align with the surrounding first-person plural forms.

topics.headline: prior patients become first-person endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the same afflicted referent from third-person description in 44:11 into first-person plea in 44:12.
topics.reason: The boundary row coheres with the local first-person plural suffix and the prior punishment context.

words.gloss_range: definite accusative verbal noun naming the known punishment as the object to be removed
words.root_gloss_range: broad root range includes sweetness, abstention, withholding, uncoveredness, torment, appendage, and other branches; the local definite gerund selects punitive torment while the sweetness contrast can sharpen deprivation

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the verb governing the punishment as object
the separation phrase naming the speakers from whom punishment is removed
the final faith predicate that follows the punishment object

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْعَذَابَ}} ({{tr:al-ʿadhāba}}) is not vague trouble. Its accusative role makes the punishment itself the object of {{ar:ٱكْشِفْ}} ({{tr:ikshif}}), while {{ar:عَنَّا}} ({{tr:ʿannā}}) names the people from whom it must be lifted. Its definiteness retrieves the painful punishment named in 44:11 and turns that diagnosis into a known removable object. The root family is wider than torment, including a sweet-water pole, but the local word selects punitive suffering; that contrast makes the punishment feel like deprivation of relief rather than ordinary hardship. The noun also sits in a same-surah punishment sequence from 44:11 through the lifting of 44:15, and its placement before {{ar:مُؤْمِنُونَ}} ({{tr:muʾminūna}}) makes the faith-claim sound like a response offered under pressure. After the exposed speaker phrase, the noun's deep opening and voiced texture make the burden sound heavy as it is named.

topics.headline: known punishment becomes removable object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the plea target a known punishment from 44:11, not vague suffering.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence mark the noun as a definite accusative direct object, while the prior verse supplies the known referent.

topics.headline: punitive torment selected from broader root
topics.reader_payoff: The reader understands the condition as punitive torment with moral pressure, not generic hardship.
topics.reason: V4 includes a torment-and-punishment branch for the root, and the local definite gerund selects that branch rather than sweetness, abstention, appendage, or place-name branches.

topics.headline: sweetness contrast sharpens deprivation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the punishment as the inverse of relief and sweetness, while still reading the local sense as torment.
topics.reason: The sweet-palatable branch is real in the dictionary evidence, but local grammar and context keep punitive torment as the selected sense.

topics.headline: punishment thread runs from diagnosis to test
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the same punishment from 44:11 into the plea and then into the lifting-and-return test of 44:15.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete same-surah references for diagnosis, request, and later lifting.

topics.headline: punishment precedes the identity claim
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears belief as a claim offered after punishment is named, not as detached prior evidence.
topics.reason: The local order names punishment before the emphatic predicate, and the co-occurrence rows cohere with that local pressure without controlling the parse.

topics.reason: Attachment evidence distinguishes object from prepositional complement, and the recitation row supports their audible linkage.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the punishment noun as sonically weighty after the exposed speaker phrase.
topics.reason: The phonetic row is local to the displayed noun and reinforces its burden role without changing the lexical sense.

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the predicate governed by the emphatic particle
the opening possessed address in the same collective voice

words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّا}} ({{tr:innā}}) pivots the ayah from petition to asserted warrant. The particle governs {{ar:مُؤْمِنُونَ}} ({{tr:muʾminūna}}), so the final clause is not a loose afterthought; it is an emphatic nominal claim offered as the reason for relief. The attached -nā makes the same afflicted speakers the subject of that claim, while the grammar amplifies their self-attestation without proving it true. Positioned after the punishment request, the word makes the prior crisis in 44:11 part of the logic: remove it because we are believers. Its nasal weight and its place in the -nā chain bind the final assertion to the same collective voice that began with {{ar:رَّبَّنَا}} ({{tr:rabbanā}}) and passed through {{ar:عَنَّا}} ({{tr:ʿannā}}).

topics.headline: emphasis scopes over the predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final identity clause as an emphatic self-attestation by the same afflicted group.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the particle with its first-person plural complement and predicate scope.

topics.headline: petition turns into offered warrant
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speakers make belief the rhetorical ground for removing punishment.
topics.reason: The inna clause follows the imperative frame and governs the final predicate, so it functions as a scoped assertion and warrant.

topics.headline: nominal clause seals the plea
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah end on claimed identity rather than on the request itself.
topics.reason: The final two words form an emphatic nominal clause after the verbal petition and depend on the prior punishment context.

topics.headline: sound binds subject and predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final assertion as part of the same collective -nā voice, not as a detached doctrinal slogan.
topics.reason: The repeated first-person plural suffix and nasal sound rows are local and reinforce the cohesion of subject and predicate.

topics.headline: emphasis is fused to the group
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that emphasis is not abstract; it is attached directly to the group requesting relief.
topics.reason: The surface form fuses the emphatic particle with the first-person plural pronoun.

words.gloss_range: active participle plural predicate claiming believer identity for the speaking group
words.root_gloss_range: root field includes safety, security, trust, and belief; the local Form IV active participle predicate selects believers while preserving security and trust pressure under punishment

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the punishment context under which the faith claim is made

words.prose: {{ar:مُؤْمِنُونَ}} ({{tr:muʾminūna}}) is the predicate where the plea lands. As an active participle plural, it claims a standing collective identity rather than narrating a single past act; the whole speaking group says, in effect, that they are members of the believer class. The root field includes safety, trust, and belief, and that range matters here because the claim is made under {{ar:ٱلْعَذَابَ}} ({{tr:al-ʿadhāba}}), where safety has been lost. The local sense remains believer identity, but the security pressure makes the word feel crisis-tested rather than settled, and the claim stands under the Lord-address that opened the plea as well as the local punishment field. The same faith root continues in Surah 44 at 44:21 and 44:55, while the word's final position leaves the self-attestation exposed for what follows, including the later return-language of 44:15 and the broader warning about belated faith in 40:85. Its internal break and nasal cadence make the final predicate sound like the landing point of the collective voice built through the ayah.

topics.headline: active participle claims stable identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final word as a claimed standing identity, not a report of one completed act.
topics.reason: QAC identifies an active participle plural predicate of the inna clause, supporting the identity-claim payoff.

topics.headline: plural form makes the claim collective
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the whole speaking group, not a single representative, bearing the asserted identity.
topics.reason: The nominative sound plural matches the predicate role after the particle and distributes the claim over the group.

topics.headline: security-root identity is claimed under punishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the tension between a security-and-faith identity and the insecurity of punishment.
topics.reason: The root field supports security, trust, and belief, while the local active participle predicate selects believer identity rather than a bare request for safety.

topics.headline: belief claim carries moral evaluation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speakers attach moral and epistemic status to themselves as the reason for relief.
topics.reason: The Form IV participial claim coheres with belief and trust senses, while its predicate function makes it self-attestation.

topics.headline: faith stands inside lordship and punishment pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final belief claim linked to the Lord-address and to the local punishment field of Surah 44.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows connect the local final word with the preceding lord-address, punishment object, and same-surah faith-root recurrence.

topics.headline: final identity remains exposed to testing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah close on a claim that later discourse can test, especially against 44:15 and 40:85.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete inter-ayah pressure from 44:15 and 40:85, and the word's closure position leaves the claim unresolved.

topics.headline: sound and suffix chain close collectively
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final predicate as the landing point of the collective voice built through the ayah.
topics.reason: The sound rows and convergence row describe local phonetic closure and the repeated first-person plural chain without altering the predicate sense.

topics.headline: nominal frame turns request into identity claim
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the request resolve into who the speakers say they are, not only what they want removed.
topics.reason: The word is the final predicate of the nominal clause after the verbal petition, so closure falls on the identity claim.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The vocative, the imperative with 'from us,' the named punishment, and the final causal assertion.
baseline_models.mechanism: The speakers appeal to an authority they call their own to remove an imposed pain, and offer trusting assent as the ground of the appeal.

activation_trace.role: Ownership and authority make the address an appeal to the one competent to revoke the condition.
Removing a cover and lifting distress supplies the requested transition from affliction to relief.
Severe pain and punishment identify what is to be lifted.
Trusting assent makes the closing assertion a pledged reason for granting relief.

changed_reading.before: A generic cry for pain to stop.
changed_reading.after: A petition to sovereign authority coupled to a declared pledge of assent.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The pairing of 'our Rabb' with removal from us and the self-description as mu'minun.
baseline_models.mechanism: Punishment can be heard as a withholding condition that disorders relation and safety; lordly nurture removes that condition and settles the speakers again in trust.

activation_trace.role: Repair, nurture, and completion cast the addressee as restorer rather than only ruler.
Lifting what covers or constricts provides the restorative operation.
Withholding and weaning let punishment function as deprivation, not only inflicted pain.
Settled safety and trust name the condition the petitioners seek to recover.

changed_reading.after: Repair deprived subjects by returning them to a stable relation of safety and trust.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The semantic tension inside kashf, the direct relation to the punishment, and the asserted faith that could be exposed as real or unreal.
baseline_models.mechanism: Kashf can expose as well as remove. The syntax keeps removal primary, but permits a second motion in which opening the situation reveals both the ordeal and the truth-value of the speakers' claim.

activation_trace.role: Emergence and exposure make disclosure a live secondary force inside the requested lifting.
Uncovered exposure to the sky destabilizes a simple covered-versus-uncovered opposition.
The claim of assent becomes something the opening may verify rather than merely report.

changed_reading.after: Open the sealed situation so relief and the claimed faith are both brought into view.

context_deltas.mechanism: A visibly emergent smoke becomes an all-enveloping cover over people. The focus imperative is therefore a counter-operation: break the atmospheric enclosure and restore an open interval around them.

activation_trace.role: Cover-removal gives the focus verb its concrete counter-cover function.
Rising smoke supplies the material that can occupy and seal the surrounding air.
Manifest emergence makes the obscuring agent paradoxically visible and definite.
A cover that generalizes over its field turns individual pain into total environmental enclosure.

structural_cues: 44:10-12 moves from manifest smoke, to its covering of people, to the imperative of kashf.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a visible smoke and a totalizing cover; I infer that kashf reverses this enclosure. A live alternative is the ordinary idiom of lifting distress without a spatial mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Remove a punishment located on us.
changed_reading.after: Unseal a suffocating atmosphere whose very visibility has become a cover.

context_deltas.mechanism: The exact requested operation recurs as a deliberately small interval followed by return. Relief no longer confirms faith automatically; it creates a diagnostic opening in which the durability of the claim is exposed.

activation_trace.role: The focus asks for the lifting whose duration the later line limits.
Trusting assent is the claim placed under the test of recurrence.
The repeated lifting grants the requested transition but does not make it final.
The same punishment remains the object, preserving direct continuity with the plea.
Smallness restricts relief into a brief evidentiary interval.
Return after departure supplies the reversal that tests whether the profession persists.

structural_cues: 44:15 repeats kashf and punishment, qualifies the lifting as slight, then predicts return.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies lexical repetition, limited duration, and return; I infer that relief tests the claim rather than ratifies it. The return could alternatively denote recurrence of conduct or condition without specifying inner unbelief.

changed_reading.before: If punishment stops, the declaration of faith has achieved its end.
changed_reading.after: A pause in punishment opens a test interval in which declared faith may either become durable or collapse into return.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same root moves among an entrusted duty, a trustworthy messenger, and belief directed toward that messenger. The focus claim can therefore function as a pledge of credible compliance within a trust relation, not only a label for inward conviction.

activation_trace.role: Security, trust, and trustworthiness make the self-description relational and accountable.
Assent remains live alongside the social pledge rather than being displaced by it.
Performing a right or trust supplies the demanded act that can make belief credible.
The messenger relation locates trust between claimant, envoy, and recipients.
The trusted messenger gives amin an enacted human bearer.
Believing the messenger makes assent directional and relational rather than merely self-ascribed.

structural_cues: 44:18-21 joins rendering entrusted servants, an amin messenger, and belief directed to him.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies duty, trustworthy agency, and directed belief; I infer that 'we are mu'minun' offers future reliability as part of the plea. The alternative is a purely doctrinal profession with no behavioral pledge.

changed_reading.before: We now hold the correct belief.
changed_reading.after: We enter a trust relation and claim that our assent will become reliable performance.

context_deltas.mechanism: Refuge in the shared Rabb stands against a regime marked by humiliating punishment and arrogant height. 'Our Rabb' becomes a counter-sovereignty claim: removal means transfer from degrading domination into protective lordship.

activation_trace.role: Ownership and authority make the possessive address a claim about legitimate rule.
Seeking refuge supplies movement into a jurisdiction of protection.
Clinging within a shelter makes refuge an inhabited relation, not a momentary evasion.
The Rabb shared by speaker and opponents contests any local monopoly on authority.
Humiliation through contempt marks punishment as a social degradation as well as pain.
Arrogant elevation identifies the rival mode of domination from which refuge is sought.

structural_cues: 44:20 invokes my Rabb and your Rabb as refuge from stoning; 44:30-31 names rescue from humiliating punishment under an elevated transgressor.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies refuge, shared lordship, humiliation, and arrogant height; I infer a transfer of sovereignty. The alternative is that these are separate episodes linked only by general divine protection.

changed_reading.after: Our legitimate protector, remove us from a degrading regime and receive us under a different authority.

context_deltas.mechanism: Night movement, a broad open gap, and extraction from punishment supply a material analogue for kashf: relief can occur by opening a route through danger and separating people from it, even while the dangerous medium remains active.

activation_trace.role: Removing a cover provides the focus operation that the escape sequence spatializes.
Clearing or uncovering shadows the commanded night passage with an opening action.
A broad open gap supplies the traversable space produced within the threat.
Deliverance by separation gives the route its successful endpoint.
Scraping out or extracting sharpens rescue into removal from an enclosing matrix.
The explicit punishment anchors the escape mechanism back to the object of the focus plea.

structural_cues: 44:23-24 sends the servants through night and leaves the sea open; 44:30 names the result as rescue from punishment.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies movement, an open gap, extraction, and rescue from punishment; I infer that these instantiate 'uncover from us' as egress. The alternative is a narrative analogy rather than a semantic development of kashf.

changed_reading.before: The dangerous condition must vanish where the speakers stand.
changed_reading.after: Relief may be an opened corridor that removes the speakers from danger before the danger itself closes or ends.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus assertion initially sounds like leverage, but the later scene cancels effective patronage and aid, leaving mercy as the sole exception. The declaration is weakened as entitlement and strengthened as vulnerable confession.

activation_trace.role: The asserted assent is the possible warrant whose force is being reassessed.
Protective affiliation is named precisely where one ally cannot avail another.
Withheld aid removes rescue as something a claimant can secure through ordinary support.
Tender mercy supplies the sole stated opening after patronage and aid fail.

structural_cues: 44:41 denies effective aid between patrons; 44:42 immediately states the mercy exception.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies failed patronage, absent aid, and an exception by mercy; I infer that the focus claim cannot compel relief. The alternative is that this judgment scene does not directly qualify the earlier temporal plea.

changed_reading.before: Because we believe, relief is owed to us.
changed_reading.after: Our profession leaves us exposed to judgment and can only be carried as a plea into mercy, not as payment for relief.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later punishment is eaten, boiled within, poured, and tasted. This activates the focus root's opposed branches of palatability and abstention: the speakers ask to exit a coercive feeding system in which punishment is made bodily interior.

activation_trace.role: Sweet palatability supplies the disturbing positive pole that punishment can corrupt.
Abstention from food and drink supplies the opposed bodily refusal or deprivation.
Painful punishment keeps the cross-domain activation anchored to the actual noun.
Taking and tasting food turns punishment into an ingested substance.
Boiling and overflowing relocate the punishment's action inside the body.
The punishment label explicitly binds the poured hot substance to the focus noun.
Tasting as undergoing or experiencing completes the forced incorporation mechanism.

structural_cues: 44:43-49 sequences food, boiling in bellies, pouring, and the command to taste.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies ingestion and tasting plus the focus root's palatability and abstention branches; I infer a coerced incorporation mechanism. The alternative is that tasting is only a conventional idiom for experiencing punishment.

changed_reading.after: Stop a punishment that invades appetite, belly, and experience by being forced into the sufferer.

context_deltas.mechanism: The faith root migrates from the speakers' identity to a secure station and secure inhabitants, while active protection blocks punishment. Mu'minun becomes an anticipated habitat and embodied condition, not only a proposition held during crisis.

activation_trace.role: Settled security is latent inside the focus self-description.
Residence and staying turn security into a stable place-condition.
Security qualifies the station itself, externalizing the state sought in the plea.
Security then qualifies the inhabitants, joining place and subject in one settled condition.
Active prevention of harm supplies the boundary that maintains the secure condition.
The same painful punishment is now explicitly kept outside that protected state.

structural_cues: 44:51 locates security in a station; 44:55 locates it in persons; 44:56 explains its maintenance as protection from punishment.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies secure place, secure persons, and protection from punishment; I infer that the focus profession anticipates a desired mode of dwelling. The alternative is that believer and secure are related root uses without a promised transformation between them.

activation_trace.role: Rising, labored breath lets the divine address be heard as a cry physically produced under respiratory pressure.

changed_reading.before: Rabbana is solely a title introducing the request.
changed_reading.after: Without losing that title, Rabbana also sounds like the breath-swollen cry of bodies struggling inside the cover.

surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Kashf acting on punishment 'from us' after the punishment has covered the people.

activation_trace.role: Open-to-sky exposure introduces vulnerability beneath the apparent covering.
Cover-removal asks for a changed boundary rather than simple nakedness.

changed_reading.before: Punishment covers them, so uncovering simply removes the cover.
changed_reading.after: The harmful cover also exposes them; the plea seeks a true protective boundary, not exposure for its own sake.

strongest_changes: Kashf becomes both atmospheric unsealing and an opened escape route, not merely cessation of pain.
The profession of faith becomes a crisis-tested pledge of trustworthy performance rather than a static identity label.
The final security sequence realizes mu'minun as a protected place-and-person condition while mercy prevents the claim from becoming entitlement.
The food and tasting sequence permits an exploratory bodily model in which punishment is forced incorporation.
summary.what_was_special: Exact recurrence of kashf and punishment with brief relief and return, the cover/opening/egress chain, and the movement of the AMN root among trusted messenger, directed belief, secure station, and secure inhabitants produced several coexisting causal readings. The split RBB mapping also preserved a contained respiratory outlier.
remaining_uncertainties: How much semantic weight disclosure can bear beside the ordinary removal construction of kashf.
Whether the amen cadence and panting resonance should remain purely poetic activations rather than enter explanatory prose.
Whether the ingestion mechanism is a genuine development of the focus root inventory or only later punishment imagery feeding back into it.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **They ask for restored exposure while claiming restored trust.** `ك ش ف B001/B002` supplies removal of a cover and emergence into exposure, while `ء م ن B001/B002` supplies security and trusting assent. The imperative answers the covering of 44:11; I infer that they identify perceptual relief with a changed inward relation. The plea reads as a claim that uncovering will reveal believers, though the sequence will test whether assent is stable.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 44:15 immediately exposes the claimed assent as pressure-dependent return, while 44:51 gives `أمين` to a genuinely secure station. The contrast corrects the plea: security is not the same as trusting confirmation, and temporary uncovering does not create either.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Uncovering asks for restored access, not only stopped pain.** `ك ش ف` `B001` removes a cover and lifts distress, while `ع ذ ب` `B003` is withholding or weaning away. The request directly reverses the smoke’s covering in `44:10-11`, after cosmic lordship and the life/death polarity (`44:7-8`). Removal therefore serves to reconnect the speakers with capacities the cover has withheld. The packet supplies cover, deprivation, and requested removal; I infer **uncovering -> restored access to sustaining goods**. The plea reads spatially and relationally, not merely as “reduce suffering.”

2. **Claimed belief is also a bid for security.** `ء م ن` `B002` is trusting assent, but `B001` is settled security and safe-conduct. The speakers predicate belief of themselves precisely while asking to be released from an unsafe condition; `44:13-15` then recalls the prior messenger, their withdrawal, and their return. The security branch assigns the declaration a possible protective function. The packet supplies the claim under pressure and later reversal; I infer **profession of assent -> expected safe state**, without claiming that motive is explicit. `مُؤْمِنُونَ` is thus tested as both conviction and a request to be made secure.

3. **The appeal invokes corrective nurture.** `ر ب ب` `B002` is repair and stage-by-stage completion. Addressing “our Lord” follows the disruptive cover and precedes a temporary uncovering (`44:15`), so lordship is invoked as the power able to restore a damaged condition. The packet supplies damage and reversible relief; I infer **nurturing authority -> repair of the covered state**. `رَبَّنَا` becomes a functional appeal to administration, not only a title.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: `ء م ن` returns as settled safety in the secure station (`44:51`) and as fearless provision (`44:55`), before protection is made explicit in `44:56`. Those later states corrected the pressured profession here: assent and security are related branches, but only durable placement and warding show them fully joined.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kanıt belirli bir bitki ya da birkaç bitki için kullanılan adı destekler, ancak bunun ağaç, genel bitki veya yumuşak ot oluşunda tanıklıklar aynı ayrıntıyı vermez. Yazın kurumadan yeşil kalma yalnız bazı tanıklıklarda belirtilir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal genel olarak bütün yeşil bitkileri değil, adı bu biçimde verilen bir veya birkaç belirli bitki türünü kapsar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım doğrudan tanıklanan bitki adıyla sınırlıdır; genel otluk, ağaçlık veya bütün yaz yeşil kalan bitkiler anlamına genişletilmez.

concept_map.definition: Yumuşak ot, başka bir bitki veya küçük ağaç olarak betimlenen belirli bir bitki adıdır; bazı türlerinin yazın kurumadan yeşil kaldığı belirtilir.

facets.statement: Ad, genel bitki sınıfını değil belirli bir bitki ya da bitki grubunu gösterir.
Bitkinin ot, başka bir bitki veya ağaç sayılması tanıklıklara göre değişir.
Yumuşaklık ve yazın kurumadan yeşil kalma bazı tanımlarda ayırt edici özelliktir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanıklıklar bunun belirli bir bitki adı olduğunda birleşir; ot, ağaç ve yumuşak yazlık yeşil bitki betimleri arasında kapsam farkı bırakır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Türün tam bitkibilimsel karşılığı belirlenmeden, kanıttaki özel bitki adını açıklamak için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Özel bitki adı oluşunu ve tür ayrıntısındaki belirsizliği korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Yumuşak bir ot ve yazın kurumayan bitki olarak betimlenen özel tanıklık için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Yumuşaklık ve yaz boyunca yeşil kalma özelliklerini korur.

error_profile.preserves: Bitki ve yumuşak yeşillik yönünü kısmen korur.
error_profile.adds: Bütün otsu bitkileri kapsayan geniş ve türsüz bir anlam ekler.
error_profile.collision: Ağaç olarak verilen tanıklığı ve özel tür adını görünmez kılar.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal özel ve türü tam belirlenmemiş bir bitki adıdır; komşu dal ise ağaç olmayan taze yeşil bitkilerin genel sınıfını anlatır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kanıt, temel olarak bol miktarda suyu ve bu adın suyun toplanmasıyla açıklanmasını destekler. Suyun tatlı olması mümkün bir nitelik olarak verilir, fakat bütün kullanımlar için zorunlu değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım doğrudan bol su anlamıyla sınırlıdır; suyu tutan yer, kuyu veya deniz gibi kap ve yer adları yalın anlama eklenmez.

facets.statement: Belirleyici özellik suyun çok miktarda bulunması ve toplanmış olmasıdır.
Tatlılık bazı tanıklıklarda olası bir niteliktir, ancak çekirdeğin zorunlu koşulu değildir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanıklıklar çok miktardaki su anlamında birleşir ve adlandırmayı suyun toplanmasına bağlar; tatlı su niteliğini zorunlu olmayan bir seçenek olarak verir.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Tanıklığın suyun hem çok hem tatlı olduğunu açıkça belirttiği kullanımda uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Yaban sığırı ve sürü olma çekirdeğini korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kanıt, belirsiz bir adla azlık bildiren ilgeci ve ona eklenen öğelerle oluşan biçimleri tutarlı biçimde tek bir dil bilgisel dalda toplar. Ekleme, sonrasında ad veya eylem gelme koşulunu değiştirir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal bir varlığı adlandırmaz; azlık veya ara sıra gerçekleşme bildiren dil bilgisel işlev ve onun biçim değişkeleridir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalnız tanıklanan ilgeç ve ekli biçimlerinin söz dizimsel işleviyle sınırlıdır; aynı sesli ad anlamlarına genişlemez.

concept_map.definition: Belirsiz bir adla birlikte sayının azlığını bildiren bir ilgeçtir. Eklenen öğelere göre ardından eylem gelebilir ve anlam ara sıra gerçekleşmeye yaklaşabilir.

facets.statement: Temel biçim belirsiz adın önünde azlık bildirir ve adı dil bilgisel olarak kendine bağlar.
Eklenen bir öğe, ardından eylem gelmesini ve zaman zaman gerçekleşme yorumunu mümkün kılar.
Bazı ağız biçimlerinde sona farklı sesler eklenir, ancak temel azlık işlevi sürer.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanıklıklar temel biçimin azlık bildiren ve belirsiz adı yöneten bir ilgeç olduğunda birleşir; ekli biçimlerin eylemle kullanımını ve ağız değişkelerini açıklar.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kanıt, aynı yalın sözlük biçimi için gereksinim, sıkı düğüm ve iyilikte bulunma anlamlarını açıkça sıralar. Dal bu anlamları tek bir kavrama indirgemeden çok anlamlı bir sözlük kümesi olarak koruduğunda kaynak kaydıyla uyumludur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Üç anlam bağlama göre birbirinin alternatifi olarak okunmalıdır; kaynak aralarında ortak bir kavramsal veya kökensel bağ açıklamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanıklanan yalın biçim üç ayrı sözlük anlamı taşır; tanım bunları tek anlamda birleştirmeden aynı biçimin çok anlamlı kullanımları olarak verir.

concept_map.definition: Aynı yalın sözlük biçimi, aralarında ortak bir kavramsal bağ belirtilmeksizin, bağlama göre gereksinim, sıkı düğüm ya da iyilik ve yardım anlamlarından birini taşır.

facets.statement: Kayıt, aynı biçim altında birbirine indirgenmeyen üç alternatif sözlük anlamını bir arada tanıklar.
Bir kullanımda biçim, karşılanması beklenen bir gereksinimi bildirir.
Başka bir kullanımda çözülmesi güç, sıkıca bağlanmış düğümü bildirir.
Bir diğer kullanımda başkasına sağlanan iyilik ve yardımı bildirir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tek kaynak kaydı aynı biçimi gereksinim, sıkı düğüm ve iyilikte bulunma anlamlarıyla tanıklar; anlamlar arasında ortak bir açıklama vermediği için bunlar ayrı sözlük kullanımları olarak korunur.

concept_gloss.applicability: Aynı biçimin üç ayrı sözlük anlamını birlikte gösteren kavramsal özet olarak uygundur; tekil bağlamda ilgili anlam seçilmelidir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kanıt, insan veya hayvanda yüksek ve zor solumayı ortaklaştırır. Yürüyüş veya koşu sonrasında insanın soluğunun yükselmesi ile atın koşu ya da korku sonucu şişmesi bu çekirdeğin farklı gerçekleşmeleridir. Dal bir arazi yüksekliğini değil, solunumun zorlanmış durumunu anlatır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal yüksek, hızlı veya tıkanmış soluk durumuyla sınırlıdır; tek başına genel yorgunluğu ya da süreğen bir hastalık tanısını zorunlu kılmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Soluk sıkışmasını adlandıran biçimler ile kişinin veya hayvanın koşu, yürüyüş ya da korku sonucu bu duruma girmesi ayrı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: İnsan veya hayvanın yürüyüş ya da koşu gibi bir nedenle soluğunun yükselmesi ve zorlaşmasıdır. Atın koşu veya korku sonucu şişmesi bu solunum durumunun hayvandaki özel bir görünümüdür.

facets.statement: Soluk olağandan yüksek, hızlı ve sıkışık duruma gelir.
Durum yürüyüş veya koşu sonrasında insanı ya da hayvanı etkileyebilir; korku sonrası görünüm at için tanıklanır.
Atın koşu veya korku sonucu şişmesi zorlanan solumanın özel bir görünümüdür.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kanıtlar yüksek ve zor solumayı ortak çekirdek olarak verir; yürüyüş veya koşu bu durumu tetikleyebilir, şişme görünümü ise atın koşu veya korku sonrasındaki özel gerçekleşmesidir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kanıt, çocuk veya ürün gibi büyüyen bir varlığı besleyerek gelişmesini sağlama ile bir topluluk içinde yetişip gelişme yönlerini aynı büyüme sürecinde birleştirir. Ettirgen bakım ile yetişenin kendi gelişimi katılımcı bakımından ayrıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Besleyip büyütme, bunun sonucu gelişme ve bir topluluk içinde yetişme kullanımları katılımcı değişimleri korunarak ayrı gösterilir.

facets.statement: Büyüyen varlık beslenir ve gelişmesi sağlanır.

Kişi belirli bir topluluğun içinde yetişip gelişebilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kanıtlar beslemeyi büyümenin nedeni, büyümeyi de bakımın sonucu olarak ilişkilendirir; çocuk ve ürün bu yapının örnekleridir, topluluk içinde yetişme ise katılımcı yönünü değiştirir.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Anlam olağan bir örtü kaldırma değildir; şiddetli durumun başlamasını bildiren sabit anlatıma ve iki alternatif köken açıklamasına bağlıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Kanıt bir sabit anlatım verse de mekanik profil çözülmemiştir; tanım bu anlatımı çıplak bir kök anlamına genişletmez.

concept_map.definition: Sabit bir anlatımda savaş veya başka ağır bir durumun şiddetinin belirgin biçimde ortaya çıkmasını anlatır. Kökeni, savaşın bütün ağırlığıyla başlamasıyla veya deveyle ilgili bir uygulamayla açıklanır.

facets.statement: Belirtilen sabit anlatım, ağır ve çetin bir durumun şiddetinin görünür hâle gelmesini belirtir.
Bir köken açıklaması anlatımı, savaşın bütün ağırlığıyla başlaması ve şiddetin ortaya çıkmasıyla ilişkilendirir.
Alternatif köken açıklaması anlatımı deveyle ilgili bir uygulamaya dayandırır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Dal, ağır bir durumun şiddetinin ortaya çıkmasını bildiren sabit anlatımla sınırlıdır; bu sonuç anlamı tek bir açıklamaya bağlı değildir.

source_details.summary: Köken bir açıklamada savaşın bütün şiddetiyle başlamasına, alternatif açıklamada ise deveyle ilgili bir uygulamaya bağlanır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Yetkili ifade, suyun tatlı, hoş ve tuzlu olmayan niteliğini merkeze alırken kolay tüketilen başka yiyecek ve içecekleri de kapsar. Tatlı su arama, suyu tatlı bulma ve iki belirli sıvıyı birlikte adlandırma kullanımları bu niteliğe bağlı yan kullanımlardır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Çekirdek tat ve tüketim hoşluğudur; cezalandırma, yeme içmeden kesilme ve sudaki yabancı madde bu dala girmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım hem yalın nitelik bildiren biçimleri hem de tatlı su edinme, arama veya öyle sayma yapılarıyla sınırlı kullanımları ayrı tutar.

concept_map.definition: Su başta olmak üzere bir yiyecek veya içeceğin tatlı, hoş ve kolay tüketilir olması; su için ayrıca tuzlu olmama niteliğini taşır. Bu niteliğe bağlı yapılar tatlı su edinmeyi, aramayı ya da bir şeyi tatlı saymayı anlatabilir.

facets.statement: Bir yiyecek veya içeceğin damakta hoş, tatlı ve kolay tüketilir olmasıdır.
Su söz konusu olduğunda hoş içimin yanında tuzlu olmama niteliği belirgindir.
Belirli yapılarda tatlı su edinme veya arama ve bir şeyi tatlı sayma anlatılır.
Bir ikili adlandırma tükürük ile şarabı birlikte bu hoşluk niteliği altında anar.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çekirdeği tatlı, hoş ve kolay tüketilen su, yiyecek veya içecektir; su edinme, arama ve tatlı sayma kullanımları bu çekirdeğe bağlanır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Yetkili ifade hayvan ya da insanın yemeden ve içmeden durduğu bir hali açıkça bildirir. Şiddetli susuzluk sık bir neden olsa da tüm tanıklarda zorunlu değildir; bu yüzden hal, açlık duygusuna veya dinî oruca indirgenmez.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal başkasını engellemekten değil, kişinin veya hayvanın fiilen yemeyip içmemesinden söz eder.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, hal bildiren biçimleri ve hayvanın, insanın ya da gecenin özne olduğu belirli yapıları ayırarak birlikte kapsar.

concept_map.definition: Bir insanın veya hayvanın, çoğu kez şiddetli susuzluk yüzünden, hiçbir şey yemeden ve içmeden durmasıdır. Bu hal bir gece boyunca sürme veya yemek karşısında belirsiz bir ara durumda kalma biçiminde de anlatılır.

facets.statement: İnsan veya hayvan fiilen yiyecek ve içecek tüketmeden durur.
Hayvanda yememenin nedeni özellikle şiddetli susuzluk olabilir.
Hal, geceyi hiçbir şey yemeden ve içmeden geçirmek biçiminde anlatılabilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanıklıklar, insan veya hayvanın yemeyip içmediği hali ortaklaştırır; şiddetli susuzluk bunun belirgin fakat her kullanım için zorunlu olmayan nedenidir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Yetkili ifade hem öznenin bir şeyden vazgeçmesini hem de bir başkasını ondan alıkoymasını açıkça bir araya getirir. Bir işten kesme ve sütten kesmeye benzetilen uzaklaştırma bu yön değişiminin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, tüketmeme halini değil bir hedefe yönelişin kesilmesini veya kestirilmesini anlatır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Anlam belirli edatlı ve ettirgen yapılara bağlıdır; öznenin vazgeçmesi ile başkasını alıkoyması tanımda ayrı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyden vazgeçip ona yönelmeyi bırakmak veya bir başkasını o şeyden uzak tutup alıkoymaktır. Sütten kesmeye benzer biçimde bir alışkanlığı ya da işi kestirmek bu ikinci yönün özel bir anlatımıdır.

facets.statement: Özne yöneldiği bir şeyden vazgeçer veya geri durur.

Alıkoyma, birini bir işten sütten keser gibi kesme biçiminde anlatılabilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak anlam, bir şeye yönelişi kesmektir; bu kesilme öznenin kendi vazgeçişi veya başka bir kişinin onu engellemesi biçiminde gerçekleşir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadeleri bu dali yalniz korkunun kalkmasi olarak degil, kalbin yatismasi, guven verme, guvenilirlik, emanet edilen sey, guvenli yer ve dayanilir nitelik alanlariyla birlikte verir. Bu nedenle dalin cercevesi, guvenlik ve guvenilirlik ekseninde hem yalın hem de yapimli ve baglamli kullanislari ayirt ederek korunabilir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalin guven ve korkusuzluk anlamlari ile belirli yapimli ya da soz obegi kullanislari birlikte vardir; tanim bunlari tek bir dar kaliba indirgemez.

concept_map.definition: Korkunun kalkmasiyla kalbin yatismasi, birine guven verilmesi veya bir kimsenin ya da seyin guvenilir kabul edilmesidir. Bu alan guvenli yer, emanet edilen sey, kendisine guvenilen kisi ve dayanilir binek gibi bagimli uygulamalari da kapsar.

facets.statement: Temel cekirdek korkuya karsi guven, ic yatiskinligi ve tehlikeden emin olma halidir.
Guven verme, birini kendi koruma ve teminat alani icine alma olarak kullanilir.
Guvenilirlik, ihanete karsi sadakat, emanet edilen sey ve kendisine guvenilen kisi anlamlarini dogurur.
Guvenin bulundugu yer, bir kimsenin emniyet icinde oldugu mesken veya siginak olarak adlandirilir.
Dayanikli ve aksamasindan korkulmayan deve kullanimi, guvenilirlik niteligini canli bir ornege uygular.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar ortak olarak bu dali korkunun ziddi olan guven, kalbin yatismasi ve guven verme alaninda toplar. Ayni iddia guvenilir kisi, emanet, guvenli yer ve dayanilir binek gibi turemis ya da baglamli kullanislari da cekirdege baglar.

facets.statement: Temel cekirdek bir haberin, sozun veya hakikatin dogru sayilmasidir.

Dini alanlarda bu kabul, bildirilen yola girme ve ona baglanma adi olarak kullanilir.

word_morpheme_spans.note: word_analysis critical words are orthographic/analytic units, not QAC words; each resolves to a MORPHEME SPAN. The upstream aligned_qac_word_ref is preserved verbatim in word_analysis and is NOT corrected here -- renumbering would fabricate identities (PRINCIPLES.md §11 / basmalah no-hidden-renumbering rule). Use word_morpheme_spans for any word-level join to QAC.

word_analysis_qac_alignment.note: aligned_qac_word_ref resolves against qac_morphemes for this ayah

channel_review.note: first-pass blind review by a single reader; no adjudication, no accept/reject, no per-ayah channel maturity. Not a channel ledger.

channel_generated_outputs.note: Generated network-v3 channel discovery/family/path outputs are available as external quran-data files; read them only when channel detail is necessary, and do not treat them as an adjudicated channel ledger.

full_context_packet.note: surah-scope fallback: the default commentary workflow does not consume per-ayah focus packets, so the source packet is scoped by this builder to roots this ayah can justify and carries no staged reveal order

scoping.note: SCOPED, NOT ABSENT. The surah-scope fallback inventory covers every root in the surah; it is narrowed here to roots this ayah can justify -- roots occurring in this ayah (all their branches kept, unconditionally, because Layer 2 selects nothing) plus roots explicitly cited by channel material anchored here (only the cited branches kept, enough to resolve the citation). A root listed in dropped_roots is a deliberate scoping decision, not a missing source.

v12_reader_responses.note: Per-ayah focus-run reader responses are retired from the default commentary workflow. Use regular reader walks, plus/minus-5 reader walks, and cross-run publication findings for corpus-wide reader-derived evidence.

v12_cross_run_publication.note: Compact final cross-run findings for this ayah, reconciled upstream from regular and plus/minus-5 reader runs; use as a coverage/priority check, not as replacement prose.

butuncul_okuma.note: no whole-surah reading file exists for this surah

occurrence_evidence_trim.note: TRIMMED, NOT ABSENT. dictionary_entry.occurrence_evidence.occurrences and .ayahs are removed from every root by design: they are a per-occurrence QAC concordance and character-span alignment table carrying zero readings, branches or senses, and they dominated bundle size (~1.5 MB for a single common root). occurrence_evidence.summary (corpus frequency) and .forms (inflectional inventory) are retained. Dictionary/gloss branches are kept in full for every included Furuq root target.

branch_policy.note: No branch filtering is applied. Every branch present in each included dictionary/gloss root entry is kept.

root_mapping.policy: Use the dominant Furuq root for every QAC root, and include non-dominant Furuq targets as additional root_lexicon entries when qac-furuq-v4-root-map marks the QAC root as split.

root_lexicon.note: Turkish is the only language with dictionary entries/glosses currently sourced.
